newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasol division looks to African ventures.
newsitem.headline: Sasol division looks to African ventures.

text.p: Sasol Ltd division Sasol Petroleum International (SPI) viewed Algeria as a key focus area as it built up a balanced portfolio of African upstream projects, group general manager Peet Steyn said.

Addressing the Africa Upstream conference, Steyn said its 20 percent stake in the El Arf prospecting licence owned by Pluspetrol in Algeria was "the first step" of its strategic decision to make North Africa one of its core areas of activity.
"The seismic programme was recently completed and a well is planned to be spudded in the first quarter of 1997," he said.

Steyn said SPI did not necessarily plan to operate all its ventures itself because in some cases "it could take up a disproportionate amount of time and effort and could therefore hamper other activities."
"SPI's objective is therefore to form alliances with leading operators while playing an active and constructive role in the venture."
He said SPI was also investigating the relatively new and unconventional production of coalbed methane in a joint venture with Amoco Corp.

"We all realise the safety hazards associated with methane occurrences in mines," he said. "We trust that through this investigation some knowledge will also be gained enabling us to improve safety standards on our mines."
SPI is also active in the Congo and Namibia.
